text:
Maya: customer reported being billed twice after a client retried on 429s. attached curl + minimal logs.

Tom: yikes. is this per-key quota or org-level?

Maya: per-key bucket. flow: client POST /v1/generate with Idempotency-Key, client sees timeout/429, retries once, both requests counted and billed.

Sophie: do both requests carry the same Idempotency-Key in the logs?

Maya: yes. two distinct request_ids but same Idempotency-Key.

Alex: probable race: quota reserved by two different workers before idempotency record is durable. gateway forwards both, dedupe happens later.

Maya: sequence from traces:

```:
1) gateway accepts req A -> router -> worker W1
2) W1 calls quota service to reserve tokens -> reserve OK
3) client retries -> gateway accepts req B -> router -> worker W2
4) W2 asks quota service -> reserve still available -> reserve OK
5) both complete -> billing increments applied twice
```

Sophie: that implies our idempotency record is written after quota reserve or in a different system with eventual consistency. where is it stored now?

Maya: in billing DB (eventual store) with short TTL. not fast enough for hot concurrent retries.

Tom: two high-level approaches:
- push a fast L1 idempotency cache to gateway to short-circuit duplicates
- make quota reservation atomic w.r.t. idempotency key (central Redis SETNX / Lua) so second reserve fails

Alex: gateway state sucks for autoscale. I prefer a centralized atomic reserve. implement Lua script: check dedupe key -> if not present and quota OK, decrement tokens and set reservation key atomically, return reservation_id. billing then consumes reservation_id.

Sophie: central is nice but note: quota service is sharded by org. our current shard key includes api_key which caused a real bug: same org but different api_key, same idempotency-key from client SDK -> landed on different shards.

Maya: fix: canonicalize dedupe lookup to (org_id, idempotency_key) ONLY for reservation/dedupe. Keep per-api_key accounting separate after reservation.

Tom: important edge-case: client reuses idempotency key but changes payload (prompt). we must detect and reject with 409 + useful info rather than returning old result for different payload. store short fingerprint with reservation.

Sophie: agreed. store SHA256(payload) truncated to 12 bytes with reservation. on subsequent hits, compare and return 409 with fingerprint mismatch details. include link to original trace.

Alex: another edge: retry storms. if we accept every reserve attempt we might run out of tokens. reservation should be subject to per-key burst cap. reject reserve if it would exceed burst allowance.

Maya: ops concern: if we add gateway L1 cache it could be a vector during retries. if we do gateway cache, keep TTL tiny (12s) and bounded LRU with admission policy. But central Redis seems cleaner.

Tom: metrics & observability suggestions:
- duplicate_charge_detected.count (by org)
- idempotency_reserve_conflicts (per shard)
- idempotency_cache_hit_rate (gateway)
- trace tag idempotency.key for all related spans

Sophie: dashboard panels: idempotency hits vs billed tokens, shard-conflict heatmap, recent 409s with payload fingerprints.

Maya: tests to add:
- regression that spins N workers, issue concurrent identical Idempotency-Key retries, assert single billing event
- payload-mismatch test that asserts 409 returned and original reservation unchanged
- cross-api-key canonicalization test where same org, two api_keys use same idempotency-key and dedupe lands on same canonical reservation

Tom: action items:
- Maya: draft gateway L1 cache spec (if we still want it) with mem limits and eviction policy  due Fri EOD
- Alex: prototype Redis Lua reserve-if-not-claimed + bench 10k rps, measure latency and memory  due Tue
- Sophie: add payload fingerprint to idempotency records and implement 409 path due Mon
- Tom: regression test harness for 1000 concurrent retries asserting single billing event due Wed

billing-bot: I can run synthetic charge workloads for test-org if you give me id

Maya: test-org id = test-org-2025. billing-bot: run 1000 rapid retries (mix 429/timeout/200) and report back

billing-bot: started :hourglass: will post results in ~6m

Alex: small tweak: reservation TTL should be slightly longer than typical client retry window so late in-flight retries still dedupe but not forever. e.g., client timeout 5s -> reservation TTL 8s.

Sophie: error payload for 409 should include: original_request_fingerprint, original_timestamp, trace_id link, and a short explanation. make it actionable for SDKs.

Maya: ok. I'll put RFC draft in RFCs/gateway-idempotency and ping this thread when uploaded. keeping thread open until billing-bot run + regression tests pass.

billing-bot: done. quick run summary: test-org-2025, 1000 retries -> observed 2 duplicate_charge_detected events. attaching minimal logs to #incidents for triage.
